title: Exportable On-Call Handoff Brieflet with SLO Sparklines & Audit Snapshot
creator: Dana Kim
description: Problem statement: On-call engineers lose precious time at shift change tracking down context (recent alerts, SLO movement, cost exposure, linked incidents/postmortems). Existing handoff flows in Console are heavy-weight (full incident pages or ad-hoc Slack notes) and don't produce a compact, auditable artifact teams can archive. This ticket proposes a lightweight, exportable 'brieflet' that summarizes the on-call snapshot and anchors follow-up actions.
acceptance_criteria: Design and high-fidelity prototype of a compact exportable brief (PDF/Markdown) that fits onto one page when printed and includes: header metadata (team, window, owner), top-3 alerts during window with time and brief reason, SLO sparklines for impacted services (7d trend), cost exposure estimate (last 1h window), linked incident threads and postmortem anchors, and acknowledgment checklist.

Console prototype supports inline 'Add note' field and preserves notes in the brief export. Notes must be editable in the short window (30m) after handoff and persisted to incident audit log if attached to an incident.
Prototype shows proof-of-concept for sanitization rules (masking PII/customer identifiers) and an explicit consent checkbox before export when customer-facing identifiers are present.

Engineering review has validated data availability and shown that requested queries (SLO sparkline, recent alert slice, cost window) can be produced within 500ms for typical team windows (50–200 alerts).
PM and Eng sign-off on required fields and export formats. UX review approved the information hierarchy and microcopy for handoff guidance.
A short playbook snippet links to the postmortem creation flow and creates a stub postmortem checklist when 'Archive brief as postmortem starter' is selected during export.
design_decisions: Keep the brieflet intentionally dense but scannable: header + three stacked rows (alerts, SLOs, cost) to avoid multi-page exports. Trade-off: limits detailed incident history in favor of faster triage.
Show top 3 alerts by impact score (severity * recency) to surface bleed-through issues; filter less critical noise out of the brief by default but allow expansion in the UI.
SLO sparklines use a compact 3-color rule (green/amber/red) with hover detail. Decision made to use 7d window for trends to balance signal vs noise.
Cost exposure is an estimated delta (1h) and not billed-accurate. Label prominently as 'estimate' to avoid billing queries. Engineering will provide exact per-token numbers in the console elsewhere.
Mask customer IDs by default; require role 'incident-operator' + explicit consent to include raw identifiers in export. This mitigates compliance risk for exported artifacts.
Export formats prioritized: PDF (for sharing), Markdown (for postmortem starter), JSON (internal tooling) — initial prototype focuses on PDF and Markdown.
Brief will be stored as an audit object attached to the incident when 'Archive as postmortem starter' is chosen; otherwise ephemeral by default to reduce storage unless user opts in.
comments: 2026-02-25 Dana Kim: Initial brief created. Goal is a single-page export that reduces cognitive load during shifts. Attached early wireframes and a short PRD. Asked Eng to validate data availability for sparklines and cost delta.

2026-03-02 Marco Ruiz (engineering): Data availability confirmed for alerts and SLOs; cost delta requires a new aggregation endpoint — estimating 3 dev days. Performance note: sparklines can be cached per team window to avoid repeated costful queries.

2026-03-04 Priya Shah (product): Suggest adding 'Archive as postmortem starter' toggle and a short checklist template defaulted to the team's incident template. Also requested branding-friendly header options for customer-facing handoffs.

2026-03-06 Legal (Jared Lowe): Raised concern about exported artifacts including customer identifiers. Recommend masking by default and adding consent UX before export. Also flagged retention policy — exports attached to incidents must respect incident retention rules.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel (design): Iterated prototype with consent checkbox and masked IDs. Added microcopy for 'cost exposure' label and a hover explanation. Updated Figma link.

2026-03-12 Engineering review (Santiago Vega): Reviewed prototype. Implementation notes: create brief render service that composes PDF from a template; caching layer required. Flagged race condition when brief attached to an incident created concurrently — engineering will add optimistic locking.
2026-03-14 PM approval (Priya Shah): Approved for MVP build. Requested a follow-up ticket for multi-team handoff when on-call rotations cross org boundaries.
